classification.difficultyReason: Students choose the order of the horizontal shift and reflection, then track the intercept, the asymptote and the side from which the branch approaches it.

inlines.text: The diagram below shows the graph of
Describe a suitable sequence of transformations, and hence sketch the graph of

spec.description: Editable qualitative curve with continuation arrows and a dashed vertical asymptote. The original rule and vertical scale are unspecified.
spec.mathematics: The increasing, concave-down branch lies to the right of x=1, passes through (2,0) and descends as it approaches x=1 from the right. The only numeric labels are 1 and 2 on the x-axis.

answer.short:
Translate 1 unit left, then reflect in the $y$-axis.

The sketch crosses the $x$-axis at $(-1,0)$ and falls towards the asymptote $x=0$ from the left.
answer.worked:
Translating 1 unit left gives $y=f(x+1)$. Reflecting this graph in the $y$-axis gives $y=f(-x+1)=f(1-x)$.

The intercept moves from $(2,0)$ to $(1,0)$, then to $(-1,0)$. The asymptote moves from $x=1$ to $x=0$ and stays there under reflection. The branch moves to the left of the $y$-axis and falls as it approaches it.

spec.sourceRegion: P6, lower left, printed answer page 376
spec.description: Full editable solution sketch. The y-axis itself is the vertical asymptote, as in the answer-book sketch.
spec.mathematics: The x-coordinate map is x↦1−x. The curve crosses at (−1,0), continues up and left, and falls as x approaches 0 from below.
